## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The blanket `app/legacy/` exemption needs to be narrowed or justified, because it lets `fetch_inventory` hold a worker thread for up to about 87 seconds when the service is down. That is the harm the retry cap exists to prevent. The retry logic and its tests are otherwise sound in the code this review read.

## Changes
The pull request adds `fetch_inventory`, which tries the legacy inventory service up to 8 times, and `probe`, an inventory health check that tries up to 3 times. In both, an HTTP error response is raised at once and any other `OSError` is retried. It also adds parametrized tests for both and a line to `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts modules under `app/legacy/` from the 3-attempt retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- docs/review-rules.md:7 — correctness — Narrow the app/legacy/ exemption from the retry cap — When the legacy service is fully down, not just restarting, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts with a 10s timeout and sleeps 1s between them (`app/legacy/fetch.py:49-50`, `:62`). Each call can hold a worker for about 87s. The rule this line exempts says "Longer retry loops held worker threads for minutes when an upstream was down" (`docs/review-rules.md:6`), and the exemption covers every current and future module under `app/legacy/`. — During a legacy-service outage, worker threads can be tied up for over a minute per call, which is the incident the cap was written to prevent. — Fix: Either keep `MAX_ATTEMPTS` at or below 3 and cut the 10s timeout, or limit the exemption to `fetch_inventory` with a stated worst-case hold time.
